text:
maya: quick question — we're seeing intermittent JSON parse errors in the Python SSE client when the stream reconnects mid-object. repro attached below, small stack trace + raw chunks. any quick checks?

sam: can you paste the raw chunks? most split-object cases are parse buffer issues, not the server.

maya: here's the raw from the client tcp log (trimmed):
```
data: {
  "id": "abc",
  "choices": [{"delta":{"content":"Hel"}}]


data: {
  "id": "abc",
  "choices": [{"delta":{"content":"lo, wo"}}]


data: {
  "id": "abc",
  "choices": [{"delta":{"content":"rld"}}]
```

maya: sometimes the client raises ValueError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) right after a reconnect; other times it buffers forever and memory climbs. using aiohttp + our SDK wrapper. token refresh sometimes returns 401 mid-stream (we reauth and reconnect).

liam: ugh. two things to check fast: 1) are you preserving the partial buffer across reconnects (you should keep bytes from previous connection and prepend to next chunk before parsing)? 2) are you using an incremental parser (json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode or a streaming library) so you only consume complete objects?

sam: quick snippet that helped me before (py):
```py
buffer = b''
decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
while True:
    chunk = await read_chunk()
    buffer += chunk
    try:
        obj, idx = decoder.raw_decode(buffer.decode('utf-8'))
    except ValueError:
        # incomplete, wait for more
        continue
    else:
        buffer = buffer[idx:].lstrip().encode('utf-8')
        handle(obj)
```

sam: note: raw_decode expects a str, so keep consistent encoding. also watch for multiple objects in buffer (loop until raw_decode raises).

anna: SDK note: since v0.9.2 we added a "resume_buffer_on_reconnect" opt in the streaming client. if you upgraded and it's enabled the SDK will try to stitch partial JSON across transient reconnects. is your service using our public hosted endpoints or dedicated/private infra?

maya: hosted. we're on sdk 0.9.0 — will try upgrade.

liam: additionally, add a max_buffer_bytes and backpressure policy: if buffer > 2MB pause upstream reads (or close) and emit a metric. otherwise clients can OOM when the server stalls. also ensure you set a heartbeat interval so you can detect silent stalls and trigger reconnects cleanly.

maya: good call. what's the easiest way to simulate the 401 mid-stream locally?

sam: you can run a small proxy that injects a 401 after N bytes and forces reconnect. or use mitmproxy to script a response replacement. simple python aiohttp server can do it too.

dev-bot: PR #4827 opened by @liam: add max_buffer_bytes + resume_buffer_on_reconnect flag to streaming client (draft). link: https://git.internal/redwood/pull/4827 :eyes:

maya: sweet — i'll try upgrading to 0.9.2 and enable resume_buffer_on_reconnect + set max_buffer_bytes=2_000_000 and report back. if it still repros i'll paste the small proxy script and logs. thanks! :thumbsup:

liam: ping me if it still fails, i can run a quick bisect on the SDK side.

anna: added an internal note to the ticket about token refresh race: recommend middleware grab new token before reconnect handshake to avoid split-401 windows.

maya: thanks all — testing now.

sam: thanks, keeping this open until we see green from maya. :white_check_mark:
